title: Validation Errors
description: Design clear, actionable validation error responses with field-level details, localization support, and helpful error codes.

data.text: Validation errors are the most common error type clients encounter. A well-designed validation error response tells the client exactly what is wrong and how to fix it, without them having to read your documentation.

items: Syntactic validation — JSON parse errors, missing required headers (400 Bad Request)
Type validation — wrong type for field, out-of-range numbers (422 Unprocessable Entity)
Business validation — conflicting fields, business rule violations (409 Conflict or 422)
Security validation — SQL injection patterns, XSS payloads, oversized inputs (400 or 422)

data.title: 422 with multiple validation errors
data.content: Return all validation errors at once so the client can fix them in a single round-trip.

rows: JSON path to the invalid field
Must be a valid US ZIP code

data.text: Support error message localization via the Accept-Language header. Return error codes that are stable across languages, and let clients map codes to their own localized strings.

data.title: Localized error response
data.content: Use Accept-Language to select the error message language.

rows: email is not a valid email

data.title: Return all errors at once
data.text: Validate the entire request body before returning. Do not fail on the first error. Clients fix faster when they see every problem in one response.

items.question: Should I use 400 or 422 for validation errors?
items.answer: Use 422. 400 Bad Request is for syntactically malformed requests (invalid JSON, missing headers). 422 Unprocessable Entity is for semantically invalid data that the server cannot process.

items.question: How deep should field paths go?
items.answer: Use JSON Pointer notation for nested objects: billing/address/zipCode. Keep paths consistent with your JSON structure. Do not use dots if your JSON uses arrays; use [0] notation.

items.question: Should I expose the submitted value in errors?
items.answer: Yes, but sanitize sensitive fields (passwords, tokens, SSNs). Replace with [REDACTED] to prevent logging sensitive data in client error reporters.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Return all validation errors at once, not one at a time.
Include field path, issue, submitted value, and constraint.
Use 422 for semantic validation, 400 for syntax.
Localize error messages but keep error codes stable.
data.takeaway: Good validation errors are actionable. Clients should be able to fix the problem and retry without reading a single page of documentation.
